# Incident Report — 2024-09-04 Traffic Analysis

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | 172.17.0.99 |
| MAC address | 18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-RNVO9AT (domain: bepositive.com / NetBIOS: BEPOSITIVE) |
| Logged-in user account | afletcher (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString, realm BEPOSITIVE.COM) |

Confirmed via ARP (IP↔MAC binding), NBNS name registration (`DESKTOP-RNVO9AT<00>`, `<20>`), SMB/browser announcement, and Kerberos traffic between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17 (WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com).

## Malware Family
**Koi Stealer** — attribution is **signature-confirmed**, not behavioral. The Suricata/ET alert log (`2024-09-04-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt`) fires `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits) directly on the POST /foots.php traffic to 79.124.78.197, which I independently verified in the pcap: 96 identical-structure POSTs beaconing to that host roughly every 60–70 seconds for the full 57-minute capture, each carrying a pipe-delimited payload (bot ID | session GUID | campaign ID | base64 blob), e.g.:

```
101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=
```
(Content-Type: application/octet-stream, User-Agent spoofed as IE7/MSIE 7.0 on Windows NT 10.0, server responds `nginx` 200 with empty body — a heartbeat pattern consistent with commodity stealer C2.)

## Timeline / Infection Chain
- t=0s: Capture opens with normal domain logon traffic (LDAP/Kerberos/DNS to the internal DC 172.17.0.17).
- t≈124–150s: Legitimate Microsoft/Bing/MSN browsing and background telemetry (noise).
- t=153.5s: TLS 1.3 session opened to **46.254.34.201:443**, SNI = `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`, ~719 KB transferred (mostly inbound) over ~102 seconds. No DNS query for this domain appears in the capture (resolved before capture start or via a cached/off-capture channel). Timing and volume are consistent with the malware/dropper delivery, though the payload itself is TLS-encrypted and unrecoverable from this pcap.
- t=155.9s (≈2 seconds after the TLS session begins delivering data): first POST /foots.php beacon fires to 79.124.78.197 — indicating execution and immediate C2 check-in.
- t=160.0s: GET `/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` → server replies `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` (bot ID | affiliate/subid | callback URL) — classic loader/stealer registration handshake.
- t=161.2s: POST /index.php with a large hex-encoded encrypted body (client→server upload, likely exfiltrated data or extended check-in).
- t=155.9s → t=3564.6s: 96 total /foots.php beacons continue at ~70s cadence for the remainder of the capture.
- t≈1224s–1387s: Internal lateral-movement/scanning behavior from the victim toward the DC (172.17.0.17) also flagged by IDS: SMBv1 use, NTLMSSP overflow attempt signature, IPC$ null-session access, SMB_COM_TRANSACTION DoS-pattern signature, and a Kerberos principal-name overflow signature — all sourced from 172.17.0.99. These match generic/legacy GPL rules (possible scanning tool or exploitation attempt against the DC from the infected host) rather than a distinct malware family, and are behavioral only (no separate CnC signature fired for them).

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in traffic)

**Command-and-control:**
- `79.124.78.197:80` — Koi Stealer C2 (signature-confirmed)

**Suspected delivery/dropper infrastructure:**
- `46.254.34.201:443` — TLS session immediately preceding first C2 beacon (behavioral, not signature-confirmed)

**Malicious domain:**
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (TLS SNI to 46.254.34.201)

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` (POST, C2 checkin, x96)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` (GET, registration)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` (POST, data upload)

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- No malware binary or file object could be extracted or hashed — the delivery session (46.254.34.201) is TLS-encrypted end-to-end and the only cleartext HTTP objects observed on the C2 host (79.124.78.197) are 0-byte /foots.php responses and small text/binary check-in blobs, not executable payloads. The only file objects recoverable via HTTP object export are benign (Windows `connecttest.txt` from Microsoft NCSI, and a 4-byte `ProcessMAU.txt` fetched over a legitimate Akamai-fronted `acroipm2.adobe.com` connection) — neither is malicious. **No SHA256 of the actual malware could be grounded in this capture.**
